analysis.title: Weekly power brief #86: Power infrastructure momentum carries into 3Q26
key_insights: With more than three-quarters of S&P 500 market cap reported, 3Q26 results point to healthy underlying demand. UBS reads the recent derating as driven by macro and AI-related concerns, not weaker earnings.
Industrial and utility reports in the Power and Resources universe show robust orders and expanding backlogs. Pricing power and operating leverage are lifting margins.

Evidence is broad across electrification, grid infrastructure, data-center power and cooling, automation and utilities. UBS says this supports its view that the investment cycle is intact and leaves room for a rerating if sentiment reconnects with fundamentals.

The Power and resources strategy fell in absolute terms and lagged MSCI ACWI in the week to 6 November. Midterm election results drove a sharp rotation away from AI-buildout stocks. Equipment and facilitator names were weakest, utilities partly offset, and US and APAC holdings accounted for most of the underperformance.

Honeywell: 3Q organic sales +7%. New orders +3% were slightly light of UBS expectations, backlog +7%, and 4Q orders are guided up high-single digits. Full-year revenue, EPS and free cash flow guidance were raised. Incremental energy orders exceed USD 1bn since 1Q26.

Johnson Controls fiscal 4Q26: organic revenue +12%, EPS +32%, orders +44%, record backlog USD 23bn (+43%), with data centers a major contributor. FY27 EPS guidance puts consensus at the low end, and UBS sees significant upside to it.

Prysmian 3Q: adjusted EBITDA +32% Y/Y and about 7% above consensus, organic growth 13.1%, margin up 200bps to 16.8%. FY26 guidance was raised again, with the EBITDA midpoint about 6% above pre-report consensus and FCF about 10% above. The company expects to beat its 2028 EBITDA and FCF targets two years early.

Vertiv 3Q (read-across, not on the list): organic sales +55%, organic orders more than doubled Y/Y, operating margin +290bps, full-year guidance raised, 4Q revenue growth guided to about 50% at the midpoint. UBS flags that durability of orders matters more than extrapolating the growth rate.

GE Vernova 3Q (read-across): organic orders +96% (Power +178%), EBITDA margin up nearly 7 points, 2026 outlook raised, buyback expanded, USD 9bn Trench Group acquisition announced. Contract signings of 11 GW were below the 13 GW expected and management guided 2027 gigawatt bookings down Y/Y, but pricing implies dollar backlog and earnings keep growing.

ABB Q3 (read-across): orders +40% Y/Y to a record USD 12.1bn, book-to-bill 1.24x, Electrification orders +70% on triple-digit data-center order growth, US orders +82%. UBS says valuations of electrification names on its list look very attractive after the derating.

Iberdrola 9M 2026: net profit +10% to EUR 5.8bn, adjusted EBITDA +7% to EUR 11.9bn, regulated asset base +14% to EUR 56bn. FY26 guidance raised to at least 10% adjusted net-profit growth, with a 2030 target of 10% average annual growth.

Vistra 3Q: adjusted EBITDA up more than 50% Y/Y, year-to-date up over 35%, 2026 guidance narrowed around a raised midpoint, and 2027 initial guidance implies double-digit EBITDA growth. Management called data center moratorium fears overstated and projects demand growth of 4-6% a year in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM through 2030.

Constellation 3Q: adjusted operating EPS up over 66% Y/Y, 2026 guidance midpoint raised and range tightened, a 20-year off-take contract signed with an investment-grade data customer, and nearly 1,200 MW of nuclear uprates and extensions planned for 2029-2032. Management called post-election pullbacks an overreaction.

Entergy at EEI: retail sales volume CAGR of about 9.5% through 2030 (industrial about 17%), adjusted EPS CAGR above 8%, rate base growth above 55% from 2027 to 2030, common equity only 10-15% of the capital budget.

Xcel at EEI: ongoing EPS growth of 9% or more through 2031, retail sales CAGR of about 5% with data centers contributing about 3 points, rate base CAGR of about 11% for 2026-2031, and data center tariffs requiring 75-85% minimum bills.

Freeport 3Q: guidance mixed. Copper sales matched estimates and realized copper was USD 6.54/lb. Gold sales of 105,000 oz missed the July estimate on shipment timing. Grasberg ran at about 67% of capacity, targeting about 80% by mid-2027 and near-full by end-2027, and the Indonesian smelter restarted in late August.

Goodman Group 1Q FY27: FY27 operating EPS growth guidance of +9% reaffirmed and power bank raised to 6.6GW from 6.4GW, with no new leases announced. Goodman and Digital Realty bought a 9.9% stake in NextDC at an average AUD 9.22/share (about AUD 715m) after NextDC's sell-off on a Melbourne power delay.

Solaris 3Q26: record revenue +55% sequentially, adjusted EBITDA +26% sequentially and more than double Y/Y. 4Q26 EBITDA guidance was raised about 8% at the midpoint, 2027 EBITDA is expected to more than double 2026, and contracted backlog is in the double-digit billions with an 11-year weighted duration. Management says take-or-pay, relocatable contracts insulate it from post-midterm permitting friction.

Effective 1 November 2026, CIO no longer rates or ranks equities in the Most Preferred/Least Preferred framework. It uses a CIO Selected designation and portfolio-level analysis, and portfolio weights are not ratings or conviction signals.

sector_views.sector: Power infrastructure (electrification, grid, data-center power and cooling)
sector_views.rationale: Orders, backlogs and margins point to an intact investment cycle. UBS sees the derating as macro and AI-sentiment driven and sees scope for a rerating.
Utilities give load growth forecasts and rate base growth backed by take-or-pay tariffs and bipartisan support. They provided some offset during the post-midterm selloff.
Freeport's results combined a continuing Grasberg recovery with less favorable near-term volume assumptions.

earnings_insights: Honeywell 3Q (reported): organic sales +7%, orders +3% (slightly below UBS expectation), backlog +7%. Management raised full-year revenue, EPS and FCF guidance and guided 4Q orders up high-single digits.
Johnson Controls fiscal 4Q26 (reported): organic revenue +12%, EPS +32%, orders +44%, backlog USD 23bn (+43%). Initial FY27 EPS guidance places consensus at the low end of the range.

Prysmian 3Q (reported): adjusted EBITDA +32% Y/Y and about 7% ahead of consensus, organic growth 13.1%, margin 16.8% (+200bps). New FY26 EBITDA guidance midpoint is about 6% above pre-reporting consensus and FCF about 10% above.

Vertiv 3Q (reported): organic sales +55%, orders more than doubled Y/Y off a +60% comp, operating margin +290bps, full-year sales and EPS guidance raised, 4Q revenue growth guided to 50% at the midpoint.

GE Vernova 3Q (reported): organic orders +96%, Power orders +178%, EBITDA margin up nearly 7 percentage points. 2026 revenue, margin and FCF outlooks raised. Signings of 11 GW compared with about 13 GW widely expected.
ABB Q3 2026 (reported): orders +40% Y/Y to USD 12.1bn, book-to-bill 1.24x, Electrification orders +70%. Schneider Electric also reported strong data-center demand.
Iberdrola 9M 2026 (reported): net profit +10% to EUR 5.8bn, adjusted EBITDA +7% to EUR 11.9bn, investment +13% to EUR 10.1bn. FY26 guidance raised to at least 10% adjusted net-profit growth.

Vistra 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA up more than 50% Y/Y, realized power prices up more than 10% per MWh, year-to-date EBITDA up over 35%. 2027 initial guidance implies double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth over 2026 midpoints.
Constellation 3Q26 (reported): adjusted operating EPS up over 66% Y/Y. The new bottom of the 2026 guidance range equals the top of the previously raised range.
Freeport 3Q (reported): realized copper USD 6.54/lb. Gold sales of 105,000 oz were below the July estimate on shipment timing, lifting unit net cash costs through lower by-product credits.
Goodman Group 1Q FY27 (reported update): FY27E operating EPS growth guidance of +9% reaffirmed, power bank 6.6GW (from 6.4GW).

Solaris 3Q26 (reported): revenue +55% sequentially, adjusted EBITDA +26% sequentially and more than 2x Y/Y. 4Q26 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised about 8% at the midpoint and 1Q27 raised about 9%. Full-year 2027 EBITDA guided to more than double 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Vistra management's long-term demand forecast supports the data center power thesis for Texas generators.
Slower than ERCOT but still positive load growth for mid-Atlantic generators.
Led by industrial sales CAGR of about 17%, driven by Gulf Coast industrial electrification and data centers.

risk_factors: A slowdown in data center capex or fading AI enthusiasm (Eaton, Schneider, Zhongji Innolight risk statements).
GE Vernova gigawatt bookings may have peaked, with 2027 bookings guided down Y/Y on a gigawatt basis.
Vertiv's record growth raises the comparison base, so order durability and margins while scaling capacity matter more than the growth rate.
Post-midterm policy risk of data center moratoria or tighter permitting and interconnection rules.
Grasberg ramp-up delays at Freeport, with only about 67% of capacity in 3Q.
Project execution or delay risk and metals price exposure at Prysmian.
Xcel faces wildfire liability, state regulatory risk and capital program execution risk.
geopolitical: US midterm election outcome drove a sharp rotation away from AI-buildout stocks in the week to 6 November.
Post-midterm fears of data center moratoria and policymakers obstructing AI infrastructure. Vistra and Constellation called these overstated, citing bipartisan support.
Further escalation of US-China tensions is listed as a risk for Zhongji Innolight.
Indonesia: Grasberg is recovering from last year's mudslide and the Indonesian smelter restarted in late August.
cross_bank_references: Schneider Electric also reported strong data-center demand, cited with ABB as reinforcing the structural AI/data-center power cycle.

tension_points.bull_case: Orders, backlogs and margins across industrials and utilities keep rising, so the derating looks driven by macro and AI worries and leaves room for a rerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterm outcomes and data center moratorium fears drove a sharp rotation away from AI-buildout stocks, and sentiment may not reconnect with fundamentals.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong pricing implies backlog and earnings keep growing in dollar terms, with orders +96% organically.
tension_points.bear_case: Signings of 11 GW missed the 13 GW expected and management guided 2027 gigawatt bookings down Y/Y.

tension_points.bull_case: Organic orders more than doubled off a tough comp, so backlog conversion is not exhausting the demand pipeline.
tension_points.bear_case: Record growth raises the comparison base, so order durability and conversion matter more than extrapolating the quarter's growth rate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to maintain delivery performance and margins while scaling capacity.
